relations.definition: To predict or estimate something, especially a future event or situation.
relations.embedding_query_text: forecasts: To predict or estimate something, especially a future event or situation.

chosen_property.label: forecasts
chosen_property.definition: To predict or estimate something, especially a future event or situation.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: expectedPrognosis
candidates.comment: An expected prognosis relation between a medical condition and its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called: anticipated outcome, predicted course, outlook. Examples: "Common Cold" expected prognosis "Full recovery within a week", "Type 2 Diabetes" expected prognosis "Manageable with lifestyle changes and medication", "Stage 4 Cancer" expected prognosis "Poor, with limited treatment options".

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: estimatedCost
candidates.comment: An estimated cost relation between a how-to instruction or supply and the monetary amount or text representing its approximate cost. Also called "approximate cost", "projected expense", "expected price". Examples: "HowTo 'Build a Shelf' estimatedCost '$50'", "HowToSupply 'Wood' estimatedCost '20 USD'", "Project 'Renovation' estimatedCost 'Approx. $10,000'".

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: estimatedSalary
candidates.comment: An estimated salary relation between a job posting or occupation and the monetary amount, distribution, or number representing an approximate salary. Also called "projected salary", "average pay", "salary range". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' estimatedSalary '$120,000'", "Occupation 'Teacher' estimatedSalary 'MonetaryAmountDistribution for $50k-$70k'", "Job 'Data Scientist' estimatedSalary '150000'".

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

relations.definition: To publish or display something, especially a message or an update.
relations.embedding_query_text: posts: To publish or display something, especially a message or an update.

chosen_property.label: posts
chosen_property.definition: To publish or display something, especially a message or an update.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: liveBlogUpdate
candidates.comment: An update relation between a live blog posting and a specific blog posting that serves as an update. Also called: blog update, live update, news update. Examples: "Election Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Candidate X wins state Y'", "Sports Match Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Goal scored by Team A'", "Breaking News Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Emergency services on scene'".

candidates.label: blogPost
candidates.comment: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entry, post, article. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPost 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPost 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPosts, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: blogPosts
candidates.comment: A blog posting that is part of a blog. Also called: blog entries, posts, articles. Examples: "Blog 'My Travel Blog' blogPosts 'BlogPosting about Paris'", "Blog 'Tech News' blogPosts 'BlogPosting on AI trends'". Distinct from blogPost, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: messageAttachment
candidates.comment: A message attachment relation between a message and the creative work attached to it. Also called: attached file, email attachment, message content. Examples: "Email messageAttachment 'Report.pdf'", "Chat Message messageAttachment 'Image.jpg'", "Forum Post messageAttachment 'CodeSnippet.txt'".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: sharedContent
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as an image, video, or audio clip, that is included or shared within a comment or social media posting. Also called embedded content, attached media, shared media. Examples: `Social Media Post` sharedContent `ImageObject: Photo of event`, `Blog Comment` sharedContent `VideoObject: YouTube link`, `Forum Post` sharedContent `AudioObject: Podcast snippet`. Distinct from `mentions`, which is a reference to another entity, not necessarily embedded content.

candidates.label: releaseNotes
candidates.comment: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

relations.definition: To express or declare something, especially an opinion or a fact.
relations.embedding_query_text: states: To express or declare something, especially an opinion or a fact.

chosen_property.label: states
chosen_property.definition: To express or declare something in a formal or official manner.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: printSection
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific print section where a news article appeared. Also called section name, newspaper section, print category. Examples: A news article appears in print section 'Sports'. The story is in print section 'Business'. The article's print section is 'Opinion'.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: articleSection
candidates.comment: A categorization of an article within a larger publication, such as a magazine or newspaper. Also called: article category, section heading, publication section. Examples: "Article 'Sports News' articleSection 'Sports'", "Article 'Lifestyle Piece' articleSection 'Lifestyle'", "Article 'Editorial' articleSection 'Opinion'."

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: orderStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.

relations.definition: To be a component or a member of something, especially a group or a whole.
relations.embedding_query_text: is_part_of: To be a component or a member of something, especially a group or a whole.

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.justification: The existing schema.org property 'isPartOf' fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

relations.definition: To make or produce something, especially on a large scale.
relations.embedding_query_text: manufactures: To make or produce something, especially on a large scale.

chosen_property.label: manufacturer
chosen_property.justification: The existing schema.org property 'manufacturer' fits the observed signature when used in the inverse direction.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: countryOfAssembly
candidates.comment: A manufacturing location relation between a product and the country where it was assembled. Also called: assembled in, manufacturing country, assembly location. Examples: "Smartphone" country of assembly "China", "Car" country of assembly "Mexico", "Laptop" country of assembly "Vietnam". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: size
candidates.comment: The standardized dimensions or measurement of a product or creative work. Also called dimensions, measurement, product size, item size. Examples: `T-Shirt` size `"XL"`, `Book` size `SizeSpecification: 6x9 inches`, `Shoe` size `QuantitativeValue: 10 US`. Distinct from `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, which are specific dimensions.

candidates.label: mpn
candidates.comment: A Manufacturer Part Number (MPN) identifying a product, demand, or offer. Also called manufacturer's part number, product part number, part number. Examples: "Laptop X mpn 'ABC-12345'", "Offer for Widget Y mpn 'WIDGET-987'", "Demand for Component Z mpn 'COMP-001'". Distinct from gtin, which is a globally unique identifier like UPC or EAN.

relations.definition: To rival or contend with someone or something, especially in a competitive market or situation.
relations.embedding_query_text: competes_with: To rival or contend with someone or something, especially in a competitive market or situation.

chosen_property.label: competesWith
chosen_property.definition: To rival or contend with someone or something, especially in a competitive market or situation.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

chosen_property.label: drivenBy
chosen_property.definition: To be motivated or influenced by something, especially a factor or a force.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: driveWheelConfiguration
candidates.comment: A drive wheel configuration relation between a vehicle and the value or text describing which roadwheels receive torque from the engine. Also called "drivetrain type", "wheel drive system". Examples: "Car 'SUV' driveWheelConfiguration 'AllWheelDriveConfiguration'", "Truck driveWheelConfiguration '4x4'", "Sedan driveWheelConfiguration 'FrontWheelDriveConfiguration'".

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: vehicleEngine
candidates.comment: A vehicle engine relation between a vehicle and information about its engine(s). Also called engine details, motor specification, power unit. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'V8 engine'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'Electric motor'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine '2.0L Turbocharged'".

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: torque
candidates.comment: A torque relation between an engine specification and the turning force of the vehicle's engine. Also called engine torque, turning force, rotational force. Examples: "EngineSpecification torque '300 Nm'", "EngineSpecification torque '221 lb-ft'", "Vehicle engine torque '400 Nm'".

chosen_property.label: researches
chosen_property.definition: To systematically investigate or study something, especially in order to gain knowledge or understanding.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: studyDesign
candidates.comment: A specification of the design methodology for a medical observational study. Also called "observational study type", "research design", "study methodology". Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: specialty
candidates.comment: A categorization of a webpage's content by its domain specialty. Also called "domain expertise", "content area", "subject specialty", "field of study". Examples: "This medical webpage has specialty Cardiology", "The research paper's specialty is Artificial Intelligence", "The blog post's specialty is Vegan Cooking."

candidates.label: publicationType
candidates.comment: A publication type relation between a medical scholarly article and its classification according to a catalog like MeSH. Also called article type, MeSH type. Examples: "A medical article has a publication type 'Review'.", "A research paper has a publication type 'Clinical Trial'.", "A case study has a publication type 'Case Report'."

candidates.label: trialDesign
candidates.comment: A trial design relation between a medical trial and the specific methodology or structure of the trial. Also called study design, experimental design, trial methodology. Examples: "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'RandomizedControlledTrial'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'ObservationalStudy'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'DoubleBlindTrial'".

candidates.label: clincalPharmacology
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a drug, detailing its absorption, elimination, concentration (pharmacokinetics), and biological effects (pharmacodynamics). Also called "drug pharmacology", "pharmacokinetics", "pharmacodynamics". Examples: "Drug 'Aspirin' clincalPharmacology 'Rapidly absorbed, metabolized in liver.'", "Medication 'Insulin' clincalPharmacology 'Regulates blood glucose levels.'".

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".
